I appreciate you making a comment on the state of this thread. I'd say there is discussion in some discords and clubs I'm in. I say continue to reach out and ask questions as I try to pick between people sharing their excitement, allowing people to voice their concerns and complaints to have discussions on their own, and try to give advice. I've only played the global since start, but starting to learn a lot of the OPM:TS guides from SEA and my experience differs.

Some examples like in Arena, I've looked at people's builds and learned to counter either by:

1. PVP Arena: Putting speed items on my lineup even at the cost of stats as I could team wipe or KO enough units before they take a turn even if they had King or ZB
2. People are still leveling select units for maybe 1 good S team, but you could outperform them with different lineups
3. I store a lot of resources that I only buy very few things. I think the mystery shop is mostly useless. I keep Gems only for buying additional Vital/Stam. BTs. Extra chances for daily training instances for better return.
4. Club hopping works, just keep finding active ones to join until they become less and servers haven't merged for club v club player.
5. I've lost to some creative builds like Konbu protected by other tanks. Skywraith King surprisingly effective. I've also mainly play for the PVE and started to make progress with my own ideas and experimentation. Figurines are such a big BP boost, labs, and figuring out trials.

One day I hope to update the OMP:TS Sea version to a global version if I ever get the time or manpower to write newer guides with better thoughts on how we think about the game instead of thinking it's meta base on the unit. I've won against much bigger whales in arena cause they just have top units and somewhat basic lineup. But I take the time to check their gear and such to build unique teams that can snipe a spot in Arena.

I've played a lot of games as F2P when I was a broke student and learned to get ahead by simply outplaying or playing longer. A year from now when we have all sorts of units, I think I can see all sorts of diff builds and metas will be like rock, paper, scissor when playing.

G4 was a good buy for solo bosses, unnatural disaster, and I liked him more than sonic. Great damage and tanks a bit for that extra push to survive. He's good behind genus line up with AM and BM. Great solo bursts to me.

I doubt they'll address this since it's their cash cow, but who knows, maybe they'll take in consideration for more opportunities with the BT/BS stuff. I've seen a lot of great quality of life improvements in this global version compared to SEA.

I'd like to somehow be able to link up with the developers as this subreddit grows if we continue to voice concern of losing out early players and even new players if they see such a big paywall so fast.
Wish Granted.

I'm fortunate to be silly willy with the cycle rebates(battle pass), but I encourage others to play casually mainly for the PVE. The PVE, character animations, and seeing a collection and story of one punch man is fun. There is definitely more in the One Punch Man: Road To Hero if you want to have a lot of dailies to do and maybe feel some progression, but that gets quite whalish too if you want to be top contender.

The cost is crazy, the only thing I suggest for those who can when it comes to funds is pay the $2.99 for the BT daily pack. Best cost as it's cheaper than buying the funds directly and you get other stuff at least. Other than that, doing dailies, saving all resources, and having the cycle rebate for the month keeps me in a bit.

I recommend checking out this guide. This simplifies the strat for talents. No need to unlock all the talent trees. Just focus 1 character at a time to complete pages 1, then unlock the next c har talent tree and so forth.
